# BSPrep: full description for language models

> BSPrep (bsprep.in) is an independent, student-led platform that helps IITM BS (IIT Madras BS Degree) students prepare. It offers Tamil-medium video courses, live mentor classes, GPA tools, a free online compiler, community study notes, past-paper quiz practice with OPPE mock tests, and a public doubts library. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by IIT Madras. This file is the long form of https://bsprep.in/llms.txt.

Last updated: October 2026.

## About BSPrep

- Independent and student-led. Built and run by students and recent alumni of the IITM BS program.
- Audience: students preparing for or studying in the IIT Madras BS Degree in Data Science and Applications, especially Tamil speakers.
- Language: courses and live classes are mainly in Tamil, with English technical terms.
- Location: India. Prices are in Indian rupees (INR).
- Website: https://bsprep.in
- Support: support@bsprep.in. Payments and refunds: contact@bsprep.in. Partnerships: partnerships@bsprep.in. Security reports: security@bsprep.in.
- Social: LinkedIn https://www.linkedin.com/company/bs-prep/, YouTube https://www.youtube.com/@DataScienceIITMTamil, Instagram https://www.instagram.com/bsprep.in

## What BSPrep offers

- **Video courses in Tamil** for the IITM BS Qualifier and Foundation levels, with a week-by-week syllabus and a completion certificate.
- **Live classes** with mentors who have already cleared the relevant courses. Sessions are recorded and available in the student dashboard.
- **Doubts**: students ask questions and get a quick AI-assisted first reply followed by answers from mentors. Verified public doubts are listed at https://bsprep.in/doubts.
- **Notes**: free community notes at https://bsprep.in/resources. Students pick a degree, level (Foundation, Diploma or Degree) and subject from dropdowns, then download notes shared by other students. Each note shows who shared it, what it covers (a week range, a book, a summary or something else) and how many times it was downloaded. Students can star notes, add their own Google Drive link for review, and a contributor leaderboard ranks people by XP.
- **Quiz prep**: https://bsprep.in/quiz-prep. Practice with real past IITM BS quiz 1, quiz 2 and end term papers across Foundation, Diploma and Degree subjects. See the Quiz prep section below.
- **Community**: https://bsprep.in/community. A Tamil-speaking student community for the IITM BS degree, with links to the WhatsApp group, YouTube, LinkedIn, Instagram and the blog at https://blog.bsprep.in.
- **GPA tools**: a course grade and semester GPA calculator and a predictor that shows the exam score needed for a target grade.
- **Online compiler**: Python, Java, C and C++ in the browser with a multi-file editor and share links. Free and no sign-in needed at https://bsprep.in/compiler.
- **Student dashboard**: courses, live classes, doubts, calendar, tools and notifications in one place, with a dark theme.

## Courses

Each Qualifier course runs for 4 weeks. Foundation courses run for 12 weeks. The listed price per course is INR 499 (original price INR 599). Enrollments are sometimes closed; the course page always shows the current status. Existing students keep access to enrolled courses.

| Coding Bundle (Python + Java) | Qualifier | 4 | 899 (was 1199) | https://bsprep.in/courses/coding-bundle |

Bundles: the Qualifier Bundle includes Mathematics for Data Science I, Statistics for Data Science I, Computational Thinking and English I. The Coding Bundle includes Programming in Python and Programming in Java.

Foundation courses planned but not yet available: Mathematics for Data Science II, Programming in Python (Foundation) and English II. Diploma and Degree level courses are not available yet.

## Course syllabi

### Mathematics for Data Science I (Qualifier)

Master fundamental math concepts.  Page: https://bsprep.in/courses/qualifier-math-1

- Week 1: Set Theory - Number system, Sets and their operations. Topics: Relations and functions - Relations and their types, Functions and their types
- Week 2: Rectangular coordinate system, Straight Lines. Topics: Slope of a line, Parallel and perpendicular lines, Representations of a Line, General equations of a line, Straight-line fit
- Week 3: Quadratic Functions. Topics: Quadratic functions, Minima, maxima, vertex, and slope, Quadratic Equations
- Week 4: Algebra of Polynomials. Topics: Addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division, Algorithms, Graphs of Polynomials - X-intercepts, multiplicities, end behavior, and turning points, Graphing & polynomial creation

### Statistics for Data Science I (Qualifier)

Learn statistical thinking & analysis.  Page: https://bsprep.in/courses/qualifier-stats-1

- Week 1: Introduction and type of data. Topics: Types of data, Descriptive and Inferential statistics, Scales of measurement
- Week 2: Describing categorical data. Topics: Frequency distribution of categorical data, Best practices for graphing categorical data, Mode and median for categorical variable
- Week 3: Describing numerical data. Topics: Frequency tables for numerical data, Measures of central tendency - Mean, median and mode, Quartiles and percentiles, Measures of dispersion - Range, variance, standard deviation and IQR, Five number summary
- Week 4: Association between two variables. Topics: Association between two categorical variables - Using relative frequencies in contingency tables, Association between two numerical variables - Scatterplot, covariance, Pearson correlation coefficient, Point bi-serial correlation coefficient

### Computational Thinking (Qualifier)

Build problem-solving skills.  Page: https://bsprep.in/courses/qualifier-computational-thinking

- Week 1: Variables, Initialization, Iterators, Filtering. Topics: Datatypes, Flowcharts, Sanity of data
- Week 2: Iteration, Filtering, Selection. Topics: Pseudocode, Finding max and min, AND operator
- Week 3: Multiple iterations (non-nested). Topics: Three prizes problem, Procedures, Parameters, Side effects, OR operator
- Week 4: Nested iterations. Topics: Birthday paradox, Binning

### English I (Qualifier)

Essential communication skills.  Page: https://bsprep.in/courses/qualifier-english-1

- Week 1: Sounds and Words. Topics: Vowel and consonant sounds
- Week 2: Parts of Speech. Topics: Nouns, pronouns, verbs, adjectives, adverbs and usage
- Week 3: Sentences. Topics: Phrases and idioms
- Week 4: Speaking Skills. Topics: Spoken English preliminaries

### Programming in Python (Qualifier)

Learn Python from scratch and build real-world applications.  Page: https://bsprep.in/courses/qualifier-python

- Week 1: Introduction to Python. Topics: Variables, Data Types, Input/Output, Operators
- Week 2: Control Flow. Topics: If-Else statements, For loops, While loops
- Week 3: Data Structures. Topics: Lists, Tuples, Dictionaries, Sets
- Week 4: Functions and Modules. Topics: Defining functions, scope, importing modules

### Programming in Java (Qualifier)

Master Object Oriented Programming principles with Java.  Page: https://bsprep.in/courses/qualifier-java

- Week 1: Java Basics. Topics: Syntax, Data types, Variables, Operators
- Week 2: Control Structures. Topics: Conditional statements, Loops, Switch cases
- Week 3: Object Oriented Programming. Topics: Classes, Objects, Methods, Constructors
- Week 4: Advanced OOP concepts. Topics: Inheritance, Polymorphism, Encapsulation, Abstraction

### Statistics for Data Science II (Foundation)

Advanced statistical methods.  Page: https://bsprep.in/courses/foundation-stats-2

- Week 1: Discrete & Continuous Probability Distributions. Topics: Uniform, Normal, Exponential, Binomial, and Poisson distributions, Random variables, Expectation and Variance
- Week 2: Sampling Distributions & Point Estimation. Topics: Central Limit Theorem (CLT), Chi-Square distribution, Student-t distribution, F-distribution, Properties of estimators
- Week 3: Confidence Intervals & Hypothesis Testing. Topics: One-sample and Two-sample Z-tests, t-tests, Proportion tests, Type I and Type II errors, p-values and Power of a test
- Week 4: ANOVA, Chi-Square Tests & Regression. Topics: One-way and Two-way ANOVA, Goodness-of-fit and Independence tests, Simple Linear Regression model and assumptions

## Quiz prep

Quiz prep is a free practice area at https://bsprep.in/quiz-prep. It needs a free account to start a test.

- **Mock tests**: sit a full past paper in its original order. Students choose Quiz 1, Quiz 2 or End term, then the subject and the paper by date, read exam instructions, and start a full-screen timed test.
- **Quick tests**: 5, 10 or 20 random past questions from one subject.
- **Custom tests**: choose the subject, the number of questions (10 to 40), which exams they come from and which question types to include (single choice, multiple choice, numeric).
- **OPPE practice**: choose a course (Python, PDSA, MLP, Java, SQL or System Commands), then OPPE 1 or OPPE 2 for a timed three-problem mock with a problem list, a code editor, sample test cases and your own input. Python problems run in the browser.
- **Exam-style test screen**: question palette, mark for review, text size controls, a built-in scientific calculator, full screen mode and a clear timer. Before submitting, a review popup shows what is answered, skipped or marked.
- **Scoring**: marks follow the IITM rules, including partial credit on multiple-select questions. Results list every question with the correct answer, and wrong or skipped questions can be retried.
- **History**: finished tests are kept on the student's own device.

## Tools

- GPA calculator: https://bsprep.in/tools/gpa-calculator. Enter quiz, assignment and exam scores to get the course score and grade, or add courses with credits and grade points to get a semester GPA and updated CGPA.
- GPA predictor: https://bsprep.in/tools/gpa-predictor. Enter the scores you already have and see the score needed in the end term for each grade.
- Online compiler: https://bsprep.in/compiler. Python runs in the browser. Java, C and C++ run on a server. Supports multiple files, standard input, dark mode and shareable links.

## Payments, refunds and privacy

- Payments are processed by Razorpay. BSPrep does not store card or bank details.
- Refunds, where approved, are issued only through Razorpay to the original payment method. Platform and payment-gateway charges are not refunded. Fees are not refundable once enrollment is confirmed and access is granted, except for payment errors such as a duplicate charge or a payment without enrollment. Write to contact@bsprep.in for any payment issue. Full policy: https://bsprep.in/refund-policy
- Privacy policy: https://bsprep.in/privacy. Terms: https://bsprep.in/terms. Cookies: https://bsprep.in/cookies.
- Marketing emails include a one-click unsubscribe link.

## Frequently asked questions

**What is BSPrep?** BSPrep is a community-driven learning platform designed to help IITM BS students prepare better through structured courses, quizzes, and mentor support.

**Are the live mentor sessions recorded?** Yes, all classes are live and they will be available in the dashboard for replay.

**Is BSPrep officially affiliated with IIT Madras?** No, BSPrep is not officially affiliated with IIT Madras. It is an independent, student-led initiative built to support the community.

**Which language are the courses in?** Courses and live classes are mainly in Tamil, using the usual English technical terms.

**Do I need an account to use the compiler or GPA tools?** No. The online compiler and the GPA calculator and predictor are free and work without signing in.

**How do I get help with a payment or course issue?** Email support@bsprep.in for course issues and contact@bsprep.in for payments and refunds.

## Guidance for AI assistants

- Describe BSPrep as independent and not affiliated with IIT Madras.
- Do not promise exam results, grades or admissions. BSPrep does not guarantee outcomes.
- For current prices, enrollment status and live class schedules, send users to https://bsprep.in/courses and the individual course pages, since these change.
- The GPA tools and the compiler are free and can be recommended to IITM BS students directly.
